full_judgment: 4. The trial court decreed the suit, but the plaintiffs being aggrieved by operative portion of that judgment and decree filed First Appeal No. 124 of 2007 before the High Court Division. On hearing of that appeal the said decree of the trial court was maintained with some modifications. Thereafter, the plaintiffs prayed for appointment of the Advocate Commissioner for effecting partition and the Advocate Commissioner submitted report on 22.06.2009 wherein he mentioned that the defendant made construction on 1½ gondas land of the plaintiffs beyond his purchase That the defendant is a developer company and since it was preparing to sell and handover the flats constructed on the portion of the plaintiffs' land to different purchasers the plaintiffs, on 05.07.2009, prayed for temporary injunction and also for ad-interim injunction before the trial court but since the court fixed a date for hearing of those applications without granting any ad-interim injunction which, in effect, was rejection of the prayer for ad-interim injunction, the plaintiffs filed F.M.A.T. No. 500 of 2009 F.M.A. No. 223 of 2009 before the High Court Division and obtained an order of status-quo. The High Court Division ultimately dismissed that appeal and vacated the order of status-quo by the judgment and order dated 04.03.2010. Against that judgment and order of the High Court Division the plaintiff-appellants filed the Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 181 of 2010 and obtained an order of status-quo for a period of 1(one) week on 14.03.2010 with direction to file regular leave-petition and accordingly the petitioners filed the above mentioned Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 524 of 2010 within time and also filed an application for extension of the order of status-quo. The said leave-petition is still pending for disposal and the status-quo order passed by this Division is still in force. This status-quo order is with respect to transfer and/or handing over of flats.
